axis: a passing piece of bad luck → an event of ruinous loss

members.tone: The lightest way here to mark a thing having gone wrong — regret at the turn events took, with no weight of loss behind it.
Meets the same unfortunate turn as *pity* with a sharper note of protest, as though the outcome were one that need not have happened.
Names real trouble while clearing everyone of it — unforeseen and unnecessary, so there is nowhere for blame to land.
Lifts the scale abruptly out of bad luck into great loss, and does it more bluntly than *catastrophe*.
The same great loss as *disaster*, pitched as total and past reversing, with nothing left to salvage.
Loads the great loss with grief and waste, asking that it be mourned rather than merely counted up.
Shrinks misfortune to one small instance, a thing to be shrugged off rather than suffered.
Ruin on the scale of *disaster* but declared in a grander, more sonorous register.
Covers both what inflicts the suffering and the suffering entailed, a weight borne over time where *mishap* is over in a moment.
Blunt and physical, casting a bad experience as a single blow taken and absorbed.
The more formal twin of *mishap*, putting the weight on the luck of the thing rather than the damage done.
